title: The Road to Recovery
summary:
The Road to Recovery
At the onset of the financial crisis last year, the fourth quarter of 2009 was targeted as the likely beginning of a recovery in the international economy. With the fourth quarter now upon us, things are, in fact, undeniably less bad than they have been. There are budding signs of life in the international economy.

children.summary: 84.4 84.7 0.3 A major factor in China's recent demand growth has been a new pricing regime instituted at the beginning of this year for petroleum products sold domestically. The system guarantees a profit for Chinese refiners and is designed to encourage them to maximize runs, presumably contributing to recent high levels of demand.

children.title: OECD‐ Back in the Saddle
children.summary: Recent economic news may suggest things are improving in developed economies but it will take a while for the OECD to fully recover from the 2009's sharp drop‐off in demand. Nevertheless, the IEA sees a short‐term demand increase within both North America and Europe.

children.title: LCC Monthly Average TCE, $/day
children.summary: The IEA's recent demand projections suggest a possible restructuring of trade flows that could create modestly more ton‐mile demand during the fourth quarter. While supply and demand fundamentals dictate that the long‐term focus of demand growth will return to the non‐OECD countries, the short‐term improvements in OECD demand present a reason for some hope amid the discouragement that has prevailed for months.
